newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open weaker on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open weaker on profit-taking.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Tuesday as early weakness in the Canadian dollar and profit-taking drove down the price of the Canadian 30-year long bond, analysts said.

"We had a great session yesterday, so there's a little bit of profit-taking in the market right now," said Harv Kalirai, Canadian analyst with New York-based I.D.E.A. "U.S. treasuries were also lower in the European session, and the 30-year Canada moved below the U.S."
Canada's benchmark 30-year long bond fell C$0.35 to C$118.17 to yield 6.594 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond dipped 7/32 to yield 6.59 percent. The spread between the bonds moved to par compared with a negative spread of one basis point on Monday.
The Canadian 30-year long bond hit a record low on Monday as North American bond prices rallied on speculation that the U.S. economy had reached near perfect market conditions.

"The near-term bias is for a positive outlook in the market," Kalirai said. "The risk really comes into view with (U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony in the second half of the month."
There was no market-moving data released on Tuesday, but Kalirai said bond traders would begin to focus on Canadian employment and U.S. producer prices data due to be released on Friday.
In new issue news, the Canadian government on Tuesday set its global offering of US$1.0 billion of five-year bonds to help refinance its foreign exchange reserves.
The bond, which carries a coupon of 6.125 percent, was priced at 99.487. The bond was priced to yield eight basis points over the U.S. Government 6.25 percent bond due June 2002.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.27 to C$109.13 to yield 6.010 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which lost 3/32 to yield 6.27 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 25 basis points from 28 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.06 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 4.97 percent.
